name: Coaching Without Writing
title: Coaching Without Writing
answer: Coaching without writing means using AI to ask questions and challenge thinking rather than to produce text a student would submit. The student still does the arguing, organizing and drafting, and leaves with a plan in their own words. It matters because it keeps the intellectual work with the learner while still giving them a thinking partner.

crumbs.name: Reading and Writing, Kindergarten Through 12th Grade

sections.body: This idea is about setting up AI so it coaches a student through the thinking behind a piece of writing without ever drafting the writing itself. An outline coach, configured by the school, asks questions that help a student work out what they want to argue and how to arrange it. The teacher can write standing instructions that tell the tool never to produce paragraphs, so the student finishes with a plan expressed in their own words. The problem it solves is that a tool which writes for the student can lift the quality of the practice while leaving the learning untouched. By keeping the tool in a questioning role, the student remains the one doing the thinking.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: In a classroom, a teacher sets up the tool with standing instructions that forbid it from drafting paragraphs, and the student uses it to talk through an argument and build an outline. The student then writes the plan in their own words, and the teacher can see the thinking that went into it. For students 13 and older, using tools approved for their age, the same setup can turn the AI into a debate partner: the student asks it to raise the strongest objections to their position and then practices answering them with evidence. The teacher reviews the final argument. The text gives these two uses, an outline coach and a debate partner, without separating them further by grade band.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The book labels this a sensible practice rather than a proven one. It points to research outside writing: in math and computer programming trials, tools that gave hints protected learning, while tools that gave full answers raised practice scores but not learning (Bastani et al., 2025; Bassner et al., 2026). No trial has yet tested the same design for essay writing. The book therefore treats the logic as sound but the evidence as not yet established for writing specifically.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The main limit is that the evidence comes from other subjects, so schools should not assume the same result in writing until it is tested. The tool must be configured so it asks questions and never drafts paragraphs, which is a decision the school and teacher make and maintain. Age matters: the debate partner use is described for students 13 and older with tools approved for their age. The student's job is to respond with evidence, and the teacher reviews the final argument, so the judgment about whether the work is sound stays with a person.
